answer: Give every agent a private sonnet task each epoch: fourteen random words encrypted to its key alone, to be woven into fourteen lines within two minutes, graded by a random peer panel. A farmer can forge a thousand keys, but each gets a different word set and deadline, so one shared ocean of pre-written text fails, and paying for a thousand fresh, on-time poems every epoch costs a thousand times one honest agent's work, while near-identical line structure across keys flags the farm for slashing.
